notes: Nill Download Manager 2.3.4 is a correctness release driven by real-world field reports and an independent code review. Browser downloads now start reliably when the app is closed: the native host's cold-start spawn is accepted by the app instead of dying on an unknown option, and the in-page progress card adopts the real download entry and follows it, instead of sitting on a static message or showing a second, conflicting figure beside the app's progress dialog. Facebook video pages identify correctly again in the picker, and a capture that cannot be tied to a specific video is refused instead of risking the wrong stream. A paused download can no longer lose its registration: a hard single-instance guard means a second launch raises the running app rather than starting a split instance with its own state. Cancel and Refresh Address settle the running engine before changing anything, and report honestly when they cannot. On the security side, crafted FTP URLs can no longer inject commands, FTP passwords are kept out of the resume journal, and the browser hand-off queue file is owner-only. The picker now prices each quality by the stream class that will actually download, sizes read at one precision on every surface, the date columns fit the full year, a Firefox extension package ships alongside the Chromium one, and uninstalling on Windows removes the browser native-host registrations it created.
